intro: Follow one sentence as the Transformer translates it: the encoder reads the whole source sentence at once, and the decoder writes the translation one token at a time while looking back at it.

steps.title: Source tokens
steps.narration: The source sentence arrives as a batch of token ids, one integer per sub-word piece. Nothing has been learned yet; these are just positions in a 37,000-word vocabulary.

steps.title: Embed the tokens
steps.narration: Each id is looked up in a learned table and becomes a 512-dimensional vector. The paper multiplies these vectors by √d_model so they are on a similar scale to the positional signal added next.

steps.title: Add word order
steps.narration: Attention on its own has no idea which word came first, so a fixed pattern of sines and cosines is added to every vector. Each position gets a unique fingerprint, and nearby positions get similar ones.

steps.title: Every word looks at every word
steps.narration: Each token builds a query, a key and a value, and compares its query with every other token's key. Eight heads do this in parallel on 64-dimensional slices, so different heads can track different relationships, such as syntax or coreference.

steps.title: Residual + LayerNorm
steps.narration: The attention output is added back onto its input and normalized. The residual path lets information and gradients skip the sub-layer, which is what makes a 6-layer stack trainable.

steps.title: Think about each word alone
steps.narration: A two-layer network widens each token to 2048 dimensions, applies ReLU and projects back to 512. It runs on every position independently, refining what attention gathered.

steps.title: Residual + LayerNorm, ×6
steps.narration: Another residual add and normalization closes the encoder layer. The whole layer is repeated six times; the final output is the encoder's representation of the source sentence.

steps.title: Translation so far
steps.narration: The decoder's input is the target sentence shifted right by one: the tokens produced so far. During training this is the reference translation, so every position learns in parallel.

steps.title: Embed the target tokens
steps.narration: Target ids go through their own 512-dimensional embedding, scaled by √d_model just like the source side.

steps.title: Add word order
steps.narration: The same sinusoidal positions are added, so the decoder knows the order of the words it has written.

steps.title: Look back, never ahead
steps.narration: Self-attention over the target, with a mask that blocks every position from seeing later ones. Position i can only use tokens up to i, so the model can't cheat by peeking at the word it is supposed to predict.

steps.title: Residual + LayerNorm
steps.narration: Residual add and normalization, as in the encoder.

steps.title: Consult the source sentence
steps.narration: Now the queries come from the decoder and the keys and values from the encoder output. This is where each target position decides which source words matter for the next word it will write.

steps.title: Residual + LayerNorm
steps.narration: Residual add and normalization after cross-attention.

steps.title: Refine each position
steps.narration: The same position-wise 512 → 2048 → 512 network as in the encoder, with its own weights.

steps.title: Residual + LayerNorm, ×6
steps.narration: The last residual add closes the decoder layer, which is also stacked six times.

steps.title: Score every word
steps.narration: A linear layer turns each 512-dimensional vector into one score per vocabulary entry.

steps.title: Next-word probabilities
steps.narration: Softmax turns the scores into a probability distribution. At generation time the model picks the next word from the last position, appends it to the outputs, and runs the decoder again.

outro: No recurrence and no convolution: the whole model is attention plus small per-position networks, which is why it trains in parallel and reached a new state of the art on WMT 2014 translation.
